shared.materials: world/materials.js — 99 procedural materials painted once at boot into a TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY (256² layers, mipmapped); shared by every arena, rebuilt on context restore
shared.noise: world/WorldGL.js — one 256² tileable noise texture (rich fbm / smooth / fine / ridged channels) used by every surface shader
shared.fxAtlas: world/fxAtlas.js — flames, smoke, dust, glow, pool, ember, spark, ring, foam, cone, flake, chunk (procedural, one small atlas)
shared.shaders: world/WorldGL.js — lit (baked light + height fog + glow + alpha cut), water, lava, cloud, planet (+gas giant), black hole, sky
shared.transitions: bosses/transitions.js — flash, fade, screen_tear, water_flood, lava_flood, warp_tunnel, darkness_swallow, membrane, armor_break, rockfall, sandstorm, ice_crack, cloud_burst (procedural, no textures)
shared.music: audio/themes.js — six archetype styles (ironclad / stratos / blacktide / helix / outerstar / drowned), phase layers p1..p5 + desperation; generated, no audio files
shared.loading: Arena worlds are built per chunk in a module Worker (OffscreenCanvas → ImageBitmap), ~0.1–0.8 s per chunk; phase 1 builds during the boss WARNING, phase i+2 while phase i is fought; at most 3 arena worlds alive (shown + incoming + prefetched), the oldest released (GPU textures + buffers) when a fourth is needed; boss art atlases are drawn lazily on first spawn and kept for the session; everything is rebuilt after a WebGL context loss
shared.referenceBoards: src/bosses/ground/*.png are concept / reference boards (art direction only); they are not loaded by the game

gaps: Audio: no per-boss music or SFX files exist; bosses use the six procedural archetype music styles (layers p1–p5). A per-boss soundtrack would need new stems per boss (30 × 5 layers).

Boss art: the 24 new bosses are procedural Canvas2D illustrations (greeble kit, top-down, lit upper-left), not painted or 3D-rendered sprites; replacing them needs 30 top-down sprites at the listed sizes (transparent PNG, premultiplied on upload) plus part sprites.
Environment textures are procedural (materials.js / paint/*), not photographic; there are no external texture files to license or ship.
